title: 5.1–5.3 Catch-Up
contentObjective: I can show I am caught up on Lessons 5.1–5.3 by using each lesson's big idea in mixed practice.
languageObjective: I can explain which lesson's big idea I used and how, using key vocabulary from Lessons 5.1–5.3.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Painting a Cabin
revealWordProblem.text: The front of this A-frame cabin is a triangle with a base of 34 ft and a height of 23¾ ft. Find the area of the triangular front that needs to be painted.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 34 × 23¾. First, 23¾ = 23.75, so 34 × 23.75 = 807.5. Then take half: 807.5 ÷ 2 = 403.75. The triangular front of the cabin has an area of 403.75 square feet.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a parallelogram. Formula: A = b × h, using the perpendicular height.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio dentro de un paralelogramo. Fórmula: A = b × h, usando la altura perpendicular.
vocabulary.visual: A = b × h; if b = 10 cm and h = 6 cm, A = 60 cm².

vocabulary.definition: A side that leans instead of going straight up and down. It is not the perpendicular height.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un lado que está inclinado en vez de subir y bajar verticalmente. No es la altura perpendicular.
vocabulary.visual: In a leaning parallelogram, use the dashed 90° height—not the slanted side—in A = b × h.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a trapezoid. Formula: A = 1/2(b₁ + b₂)h.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio dentro de un trapecio. Fórmula: A = 1/2(b₁ + b₂)h.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a triangle. Formula: A = 1/2bh, using the perpendicular height.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio dentro de un triángulo. Fórmula: A = 1/2bh, usando la altura perpendicular.
vocabulary.visual: A = 1/2bh; if b = 8 and h = 5, A = 20 square units.

vocabulary.definition: A four-sided shape with two pairs of parallel sides.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura de cuatro lados con dos pares de lados paralelos.
vocabulary.visual: Think of a leaning door — the top and bottom are parallel, and the two sides are parallel, like a slanted rectangle
vocabulary.cloze: A quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel sides is a ___.

examples.text: A slanted four-sided shape with both pairs of sides parallel
examples.why: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
A triangle has three sides, not two pairs of parallel sides.

vocabulary.definition: A side of the shape you use to find the area.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un lado de la figura que usas para hallar el área.
vocabulary.visual: If the bottom of a parallelogram is 10 cm, then b = 10 cm in the formula A = b × h
vocabulary.cloze: Any side of a parallelogram used to calculate its area is the ___.

vocabulary.definition: A four-sided shape with just one pair of parallel sides.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura de cuatro lados con solo un par de lados paralelos.
vocabulary.visual: A table top wider than the bottom shelf — the top and bottom edges are parallel, the two sides slant inward
vocabulary.cloze: A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides is a ___.

examples.text: A four-sided shape with one pair of parallel sides
examples.why: It has exactly one pair of parallel sides.
A rectangle has two pairs of parallel sides.

vocabulary.definition: One of the two parallel sides of a trapezoid.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Uno de los dos lados paralelos de un trapecio.
vocabulary.visual: If the bottom of the trapezoid is 10 ft, then b₁ = 10 ft in the formula A = ½(b₁ + b₂) × h
vocabulary.cloze: One of the two parallel sides of a trapezoid is ___.

vocabulary.definition: The straight-up distance from the base to the top corner.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia recta desde la base hasta la esquina de arriba.
vocabulary.visual: A dashed vertical line from the top point straight down to the base at a 90° angle — like dropping a plumb line
vocabulary.cloze: The perpendicular distance from the base to the opposite vertex is the ___.

launch.narrative: Missed a lesson — or just want a refresher? This catch-up station reviews Lessons 5.1–5.3: 5.1 Area of Parallelograms, 5.2 Area of Trapezoids, 5.3 Area of Triangles. Read the Big Ideas, warm up with the review problem, then prove you're caught up in the mixed practice.

conceptIntro.heading: The Big Ideas — Lessons 5.1–5.3
conceptIntro.intro: Here is the one thing to remember from each lesson, plus a quick guided example. If one of these feels shaky, that lesson is right above this one in the menu — you can open it any time.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: 5.1: Area of a parallelogram = base × height, where the height is the straight-up (perpendicular) distance, NOT the slanted side. • 5.2: Area of a trapezoid = ½ × (base 1 + base 2) × height. We add the two bases first, then take half. • 5.3: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height. A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height.

iDo.title: The Big Ideas (one per lesson)
lines: Lesson 5.1 — Area of Parallelograms: Area of a parallelogram = base × height, where the height is the straight-up (perpendicular) distance, NOT the slanted side.
Lesson 5.2 — Area of Trapezoids: Area of a trapezoid = ½ × (base 1 + base 2) × height. We add the two bases first, then take half.
Lesson 5.3 — Area of Triangles: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height. A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height.

youDo.title: Show you're caught up
lines: The practice below mixes problems from Lessons 5.1–5.3. Each problem is tagged with its lesson number.
Stuck on one lesson's problems? Open that lesson from the curriculum menu for the full re-teach.

explore.instructions: Plot the vertices of a triangle with base 12 and height 8 to visualize the garden. Place points at (0, 0), (12, 0), and (6, 8).
explore.label: Plot the three vertices of the triangular garden bed.

discourse.prompt: The triangle fits inside a 12 × 8 rectangle. How does the triangle's area compare to the rectangle's area?
discourse.sentenceFrame: The area of the triangle is ___ the rectangle because A = 1/2 × ___ × ___ = ___ square feet.

optional.stem: (Lesson 5.1) Cut the slanted end off a parallelogram and slide it to the other side. What shape forms, and why does that show A = base × height?
choices: A rectangle with the same base and height, so its area equals base x height
A bigger parallelogram, so the area gets larger
A triangle, so the area is cut in half
A square, so all four sides must be equal
optional.explanation: Sliding the cut triangle turns the parallelogram into a rectangle that keeps the same base and height. A rectangle's area is base x height, so the parallelogram's area is base x height too.
choiceFeedback: Does cutting and moving a piece change how much space is covered?
The rearranged shape still has the same area as before.
After rearranging, do you have three sides or four?

optional.stem: (Lesson 5.2) Blueprint 1: A trapezoidal lobby window has bases of 6 ft and 10 ft and a height of 4 ft. What is its area for the glass order?
choiceFeedback: What do you multiply and divide for a triangle?
The formula has both multiplication and division.
Triangle area = ½ × base × height, not base + height.

optional.stem: (Lesson 5.3) A triangular window in the firm's lobby has a base of 10 ft and a height of 6 ft. What is its area?
optional.explanation: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 6 = ½ × 60 = 30 sq ft. The triangle is half of the 10 × 6 = 60 rectangle it fits inside.
choiceFeedback: One pair of parallel sides = trapezoid.
Does this have one or two pairs?
Check which sides actually match up parallel.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 5.1) What is the area of a parallelogram with base 10 cm and height 7 cm?
choiceFeedback: Did you add? The formula multiplies base and height.
You found 10 + 7; try multiplying instead.
hints: You know both the base (10 cm) and the height (7 cm) — this is a direct use of the parallelogram area formula.
Area of a parallelogram is A = base × height. Adding the two numbers gives perimeter-style thinking, not area.
Set up A = 10 × 7 and multiply. Label your result in square centimeters.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 5.1) A parallelogram has an area of 54 sq ft and a base of 9 ft. What is the height?
choiceFeedback: Work backwards: if A = b × h and A = 54, h = 54 ÷ 9.
54 + 9 is too large for the height.
Is the height half of 54?
hints: This time you're given the area (54 sq ft) and the base (9 ft) — the height is the missing piece.
Start from A = b × h. To undo a multiplication, divide: h = A ÷ b.
Write 54 = 9 × h, then divide 54 by 9 to find the height in feet.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 5.2) What is the area of a trapezoid with bases 6 cm and 10 cm, and height 4 cm?
choiceFeedback: Multiply 10 × 12 = 120, then divide by 2.
60 is half the rectangle area.
Did you skip the ÷ 2 step?
hints: A trapezoid has two bases (6 cm and 10 cm) plus a height (4 cm) — all three belong in the formula.
Use A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h: add the bases first, then multiply by the height, then take half.
Add 6 + 10 to get the base sum, multiply that by 4, then cut the result in half.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 5.2) A trapezoid has an area of 45 sq ft, bases of 7 ft and 11 ft. What is the height?
choiceFeedback: Double the area: 2 × 72 = 144.
Then divide by height: 144 ÷ 12.
Or use: base = (2 × area) ÷ height.
hints: You already know the area (45 sq ft) and both bases (7 ft and 11 ft) — the height is what's missing.
Simplify first: ½ × (7 + 11) = 9. So the equation becomes 45 = 9 × h.
Divide 45 by 9 to find the height in feet.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 5.3) What is the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm?
approaching.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 square centimeters.
choiceFeedback: Add 5 + 9, divide result by 2, then × 4.
The bases are the parallel sides.
Follow A = (b₁ + b₂) ÷ 2 × h exactly.
hints: You have a base of 10 cm and a height of 6 cm — a triangle needs only those two, plus one special step.
A triangle is half of a rectangle: use A = ½ × b × h. If you only multiply, your answer is twice too big.
Multiply 10 × 6, then take half of the product. Area units are square centimeters.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 5.3) A triangle has an area of 24 sq ft and a base of 8 ft. What is the height?
choiceFeedback: Add the bases: 6 + 8 = 14.
Divide by 2, then multiply by 5.
Do not forget any step.
hints: The area (24 sq ft) and base (8 ft) are given — you're solving backwards for the height.
Simplify first: ½ × 8 = 4, so the equation becomes 24 = 4 × h.
Divide 24 by 4 to find the height in feet.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 5.1) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the parallelogram
workedExample.work: base = 9 cm, slanted side = 10 cm, height = 6 cm

onLevel.correctWork: The height is 6 cm, not the slanted side of 10 cm. Substitute the perpendicular height: A = 9 × 6 = 54 sq cm. Only the straight-up height belongs in A = base × height.
hints: Look at the substitution step. Which number was used for the height — the slanted side or the real height?
The height must be perpendicular (a 90° angle) to the base. The 10 cm slanted side is not the height, so use 6 cm: A = 9 × 6 = 54 sq cm.

onLevel.hint: Use A = b x h to find area; use h = A / b to find missing height.
hints: Check each row: Patios A and D are missing area, but Patios B and C are missing a base or a height.
Missing area → multiply b × h. Missing base or height → divide the area by the measurement you know.
For Patio B: 56 = 8 × h, so divide 56 by 8. For Patio A, multiply 14 × 9.
onLevel.title: (Lesson 5.1) Review problem
(Lesson 5.2) Using the Wrong Height

workedExample.label: Read the blueprint
workedExample.work: A trapezoid window has b1 = 7 ft and b2 = 13 ft. The slanted side measures 10 ft, and the straight-up height between the bases is 6 ft.

onLevel.correctWork: The student used the slanted side (10 ft) as the height instead of the true perpendicular height (6 ft). The height in the trapezoid formula must be measured straight up between the two bases, not along the slanted side. The correct area is A = ½ × (7 + 13) × 6 = ½ × 20 × 6 = 60 sq ft, not 100 sq ft.
hints: Look at which measurement was used for h. Is it the straight-up distance between the bases, or the slanted edge?
The height must form a right angle with both bases. A slanted side is longer than the true height and will make the area too big.

onLevel.hint: Use A = 1/2 x b x h for each triangle; work backwards if needed.
hints: Windows A and B are missing area, but Windows C and D are missing a base — those need backwards work.
Missing area: ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Missing base: double the area, divide by the height, then subtract the base you know.
Window C: 2 × 72 = 144, then 144 ÷ 8 = 18 is the base sum — subtract the 10 ft base to get Base 2.
onLevel.title: (Lesson 5.2) Review problem
(Lesson 5.3) Spot the Common Mistake
onLevel.correctWork: There is only ONE ½ in the formula, not two. The student halved both the base and the height. Multiply base × height first, then take half just once: 12 × 7 = 84, then ½ × 84 = 42 sq ft.
hints: How many times does the ½ appear in A = ½ × base × height — once or twice?
Multiply 12 × 7 = 84 first, then take half a single time: ½ × 84 = 42 sq ft.

onLevel.hint: Use A = ½ × b × h; work backwards for missing values.
hints: Gardens A and D are missing area; Gardens B and C are missing a base or height — those need backwards steps.
Missing area: ½ × b × h. Missing base or height: double the area first, then divide by the measurement you know.
Garden B: double 27 to get 54, then divide 54 by the base 9 to find the height.
onLevel.title: (Lesson 5.3) Review problem

extending.title: (Lesson 5.1) Find the Area Error

workedExample.label: Identify base and height
workedExample.work: b = 11 m, slant side = 8 m, h = 6 m

extending.correctWork: The height is 6 m, not the slant side of 8 m. A = 11 × 6 = 66 sq m. Always use the perpendicular height, not the slanted side.
hints: Look at Step 3. Which value should be used for h — the slant side or the height?
The height must be perpendicular to the base. The slant side is not the height.

extending.title: (Lesson 5.2) Find the Area Error

workedExample.label: Identify the bases and height
workedExample.work: b₁ = 10 m, b₂ = 6 m, h = 7 m

extending.correctWork: The student forgot to multiply by ½. A = ½ × 16 × 7 = ½ × 112 = 56 sq m.
hints: Look at Step 4. What happened to the ½?
The student skipped the ½ and just multiplied (b₁ + b₂) × h.

extending.title: (Lesson 5.3) Find the Area Error
extending.correctWork: 14 × 9 = 126, then ½ × 126 = 63 sq m. The student added 14 + 9 = 23 instead of multiplying 14 × 9 = 126.
hints: Look at Step 4. What operation should happen between 14 and 9?
14 × 9 ≠ 23. The student added instead of multiplied.

optionalActivity.name: Catch-Up Challenge
optionalActivity.intro: Mix it up: pick the right lesson's big idea for each problem — that's the real catch-up skill.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Area of Triangles is forgetting the ½ — students multiply base × height like a rectangle and stop there, or they use the triangle's slanted side instead of the perpendicular height that's already given. Always check: did I take half, and did I use the straight-up height, not the slanted side?

diagram.title: A-Frame Wall Triangle
diagram.caption: Plot the wall's corners: the base A to B is 20 ft and the height up to peak C is 14 ft, so area = 1/2 x 20 x 14 = 140 sq ft.

connect.scenario: A homeowner wants to paint one triangular wall of an A-frame cabin. The wall has a base of 20 feet and a height of 14 feet. One can of paint covers 50 square feet.
connect.promptQuestion: How many cans of paint does the homeowner need?
connect.prompt: The wall's area is ___ sq ft because A = 1/2 × ___ × ___. She needs ___ cans because ___ ÷ 50 = ___.

exitTicket.stem: (Catch-up check, from Lesson 5.2) A trapezoid has bases of 9 inches and 5 inches, and a height of 6 inches. What is its area?
exitTicket.explanation: A = 1/2 x (b1 + b2) x h = 1/2 x (9 + 5) x 6 = 1/2 x 14 x 6 = 42 square inches.
choiceFeedback: Don't forget the ½ — add the bases, times height, then halve.
Add both bases (9 + 5) before multiplying by height and ½.
Right value, wrong unit — area uses square inches.
hints: This trapezoid gives you both bases (9 in and 5 in) and the height (6 in) — all three go in the formula.
Use A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h and keep the ½; without it your answer comes out doubled.
Add 9 + 5 = 14, multiply by 6, then take half. Label the result in square inches.

questions.stem: A trapezoid has an area of 45 sq ft, bases of 7 ft and 11 ft. What is the height?
What is the area of a trapezoid with bases 6 cm and 10 cm, and height 4 cm?
A trapezoid has bases of 5 in and 9 in, and a height of 6 in. What is its area?
What is the first step when finding the area of a trapezoid?
choices: Subtract the shorter base from the longer base
questions.explanation: The formula is A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. The first step is to add the two parallel bases.
